en: Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Now begins the ritual procedure for the worship of Śrī Dakṣiṇakālī.
Taking a water vessel in hand, one goes to the door of the shrine and recites: *Oṃ vajrodake hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. With this [mantra], [the ground is sprinkled].

Having taken one's place in the water, having spread a seat there, and having sprinkled the seat with "phaṭ," one sits down. Having washed both hands and feet with "Oṃ hrīṃ, O you who pacify all sins, remove all conceptual constructions, hūṃ," and having sipped water three times with "Hrīṃ ācamana oṃ hrīṃ svāhā," [one says] "Oṃ."

Having wiped the lips twice and washed the hands with *hrīṃ*, one should touch the mouth, both nostrils, both ears, the navel, the heart, the head, and the two shoulders with the *tattvamudrā* while reciting *hrīṃ*.
Having thus performed the ritual sipping of water (*ācamana*) twice, [one recites]: *oṃ maṇidhari vajriṇi mahāpratisare rakṣa rakṣa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*.
With this [mantra], one should tie a topknot, or else tie a knot in the hem of one’s garment.

Then, one should perform the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) with the mantra: *klīṃ svāhā*. One should drink this three times. With *krīṃ kālyai namaḥ* and *krīṃ kapālinyai namaḥ*, one should wipe both hands twice. With *krīṃ kullāyai namaḥ*, [one should wipe] the hands.

One should wash [the ground]. *Oṃ rakṣa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Having thus purified the ground, one should strike the earth with the left foot while reciting: *Oṃ pavitravajrabhūme hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*, and then worship the maṇḍala in the four directions: *Oṃ vāstvīśāya namaḥ*; *Oṃ brahmaṇe namaḥ*; *Oṃ*...

Dispel all obstacles, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! Then one should recite the mantra: oṃ glūṃ slūṃ plūṃ gāṃ gaṇapataye namaḥ. Then one should perform the purification of consciousness (*saṃvit-sādhana*). Now follows the purification of consciousness.
Oṃ āsurekhe vajrarekhe hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Having thus drawn the maṇḍala in the four directions with this [mantra], one should then perform the ritual application (viniyoga):
Oṃ, of this Śrī Saṃvit, of this mantra, Dakṣiṇāmūrti is the seer (ṛṣi), Paṅkti is the meter (chandas), and Sadāśiva is the deity.
The application is for the imposition of the presence of the deity through consciousness. Now, as for the visualization:
[one should meditate on] Bhairavī, the enchantress of Śiva, beginning with the Siddhas, who holds a noose and a goad shining in her hands.
She is skilled at bestowing the desired fruits upon her devotees and severing the bonds of saṃsāra.

One should meditate upon Suvijayā, who enchants the world, who is the abode of the play of consciousness, whose essence arose from the churning of the ocean of nectar, and whose sandals are worshipped by heroes.
Having meditated thus, one should purify each [item] as follows:
Oṃ! O Saṃvid, born of Brahman, daughter of Brahman, ever sinless;
for the sake of the satisfaction of the Bhairavas, be forever pure.
Oṃ, obeisance to Brāhmaṇī, svāhā. || 1 ||
Oṃ! O Goddess who is the root of accomplishment and action, you who awaken those of inferior understanding;
you who bring kings and subjects under control, and who wield the trident against the throats of enemies!
Aiṃ, obeisance to the Kṣatriya woman; Svāhā! || 2 ||
Oṃ! O blazing fire of ignorance, O fire of knowledge, whose very form is knowledge;
considering this offering of bliss, grant me perfect wisdom.
Hrīṃ, salutation to Vaiśyā, Svāhā. || 3 ||
Oṃ! I pay homage, I pay homage to you, O Goddess who reveals the path of yoga!
O Mother, victorious over the three worlds, grant me the attainment of meditative absorption.
Klīṃ, obeisance to the Śūdrā woman, svāhā. || 4 ||
Then, with *hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛtavarṣiṇi mahatprakāśayukte amṛtaṃ śrāvaya (2) śrīmaddakṣiṇakālikāṃ me vaśamānaya svāhā | phaṭ*, perform the sprinkling (*saṃprokṣa*).

With *hūṃ*, perform the veiling (*avaguṇṭhya*). With *vaṃ* and the cow-seal (*dhenumudrā*), render it nectar (*amṛtīkṛtya*). [Perform this] with the root-mantra (*mūla*) and the womb-seal (*yonimudrā*).

Having kindled [the fire] with the mantras of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), having performed the ritual integration (*sakalīkaraṇa*), and having covered [it] with the fish-seal (*matsyamudrā*), one should recite the root mantra (*mūlamantra*) ten times therein. One should purify the distinctions of the castes (*jātibheda*) through knowledge by means of the mantra beginning with *hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ amṛte amṛtodbhave*. Then, one should perform the libation (*tarpaṇa*): *aiṃ hrīṃ*.
"Śrīṃ! Amukānandanātha, Amukī Devyambā, I satiate the venerable sandals; obeisance!

Having thus performed the libation three times upon the head, [one recites]: "Aiṃ Śrīṃ! I satiate the Gurus; obeisance! Aiṃ! I satiate the Paramagurus; obeisance! Aiṃ! I satiate the Parāparagurus; obeisance!"

"Oṃ, I satiate the supreme gurus; obeisance. Having thus satiated [them] once each upon the head, then, having uttered the root mantra at the heart: "I satiate the illustrious Dakṣiṇakālikā; svāhā. Having thus satiated her three times, and having uttered the Mahākāla mantra: "I satiate the illustrious Mahākālabhairava; obeisance. Thus.

Having recited the root mantra three times for the purpose of satiation, [one says]: "I satiate the venerable Dakṣiṇakālikā, together with her weapons, her vehicle, and her retinue, accompanied by the venerable Mahākālabhairava; svāhā!
Having thus satiated [her] three times, one holds the Vijayā vessel with the left hand using the *tattva-mudrā*, while with the right...

Taking water and reciting the root mantra: "I offer this Vijayā to the illustrious Dakṣiṇakālikā. Having thus offered it, having recited the root mantra as many times as one is able, having presented it, and having prostrated, one should serve it to the Śaktis and Vīras present there, take it to one's own vessel, and then meditate upon it, praise it, and pay homage.
Having washed the argha vessel with "KUṂ PHAṬ" and placed it upon the support with "NAMAḤ," [one should recite] "AṂ."

"Salutation to the solar disc, whose self consists of twelve kalās. Having thus worshipped the arghya vessel, [say] "Salutation! and fill it with water. "Um, salutation to the lunar disc, whose self consists of sixteen kalās. Having thus worshipped the water, [proceed].
Oṃ, Gaṅgā and Yamunā, Godāvarī and Sarasvatī, Narmadā, Sindhu, and Kāverī— be present in this water!
Come, O Gaṅgā, salutations to you who are endowed with all sacred fords (tīrthas)!
O Sun, the sacred fords within the belly of the universe are upon the palms and backs of your hands.
"By that truth, O Goddess, grant me a holy bathing place (tīrtha), O Divākara!
Having thus invoked the holy places there with the *aṅkuśa-mudrā*,

and having offered sandalwood paste, flowers, bilva leaves, *dūrvā* grass, and unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*) while reciting "Oṃ," and having veiled [them] with "Hūṃ," [he should seal them] with the "Vaṃ" and the *dhenu-mudrā*.
Having rendered it nectar with the *matsyamudrā* and covered it, one should recite "Oṃ" ten times there;
this is the general *arghya*. Having sprinkled the door with that water, one should worship the deities of the door as follows:
on the upper part of the door, these scents and flowers—"Gāṃ, obeisance to Gaṇeśa"; on the left, "Kṣāṃ..."
Salutation to Kṣetrapāla. To the south, salutation to Vaṭuka (Vāṃ). Below, salutation to the Yoginīs (Yāṃ).
In the upper-left corner, salutation to Gaṅgā (Gāṃ). Likewise, to the south, salutation to Yamunā (Yāṃ).
In the lower left corner: *Śrīlakṣmyai namaḥ*. Likewise, in the right: *Aiṃ Sarasvatyai namaḥ*.

On the threshold: *Oṃ Astrāya namaḥ*. Thus, one should worship everywhere with perfumes, flowers, and water. Then, contracting the left limb and placing the right foot forward, one should touch the right door-jamb.
Having entered within the pavilion:
"O spirits who dwell upon the earth, may you depart!
May those spirits who create obstacles perish by the command of Śiva!"

Having scattered [the offerings] in the cardinal and intermediate directions with these two mantras, and having given three upward claps of the hands (*tāla*) with "phaṭ," one should utter the root mantra followed by "astrāya phaṭ" and dispel those obstacles in the atmosphere with water. Then, with "phaṭ," one should dispel the terrestrial obstacles by striking the earth three times with the heel of the left foot. Therein—

Having drawn a triangular mandala, [offering] these perfumes and flowers, and having worshipped the mandala with "Hrīṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti," one should spread the prescribed seat there. Having inscribed the seed-syllable *hsauḥ* there and placed three blades of *dūrvā* grass, one should purify the seat. Holding the seat with palms joined in reverence, [one recites] for this seat...
For the mantra, Merupṛṣṭha is the seer (ṛṣi), Sutala is the meter (chandaḥ), Kūrma is the deity (devatā), and its application (viniyoga) is for the placement of the seat.
Oṃ! O Earth, by you the worlds are supported; O Goddess, you are supported by Viṣṇu.
And you should always hold me and make the seat pure.

Having recited this, and having worshipped the seat with "Oṃ, these perfumes and flowers, Hsrauṃḥ! Salutation to the Lotus Throne of the Support-Power (Ādhāraśakti)," one should place three blades of *kuśa* grass there, establish the general *arghya* water, and [sprinkle] oneself with that water.

Having sprinkled the articles of worship and again consecrated the sacrificial materials with the root mantra, one should purify the flowers. Having empowered the flower with this: "O Beloved Refuge, at the time of the hundredfold consecration, *śatābhiṣeka hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*," [one should say]: "Oṃ, to the King Puṣpaketu, worthy of the hundredfold [consecration], perfectly..."

For the sake of connection: *Hūṃ puṣpe mahāpuṣpe supuṣpe puṣpasambhave puṣpasamcayāvasaṃkīrṇe hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Thus, having consecrated the flowers with this mantra at the end of the root [mantra], and having sprinkled the articles of worship with *phaṭ*, one should transform them into nectar (*amṛta*) by means of the *dhenumudrā* and the syllable *vaṃ*. Then...

Having purified both hands with scented water, flowers, and unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*) while reciting *hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*, one should cast those flowers toward the southwest while reciting *phaṭ*. Then, having performed three successive upward claps of the hands while reciting *phaṭ*, one should effect the binding of the ten directions with snapping gestures (*choṭikā*). Finally, one should offer a stream of water in the cardinal and intermediate directions while reciting *raṃ*.
Having visualized the enclosure of fire surrounding [the site], one should perform breath control (prāṇāyāma) as follows:
holding the right nostril with the right thumb while reciting "krīṃ" sixteen times through the left nostril.

Having filled the breath with air and holding both nostrils with the thumb, ring finger, and little finger, one should perform the retention of breath (kumbhaka) while reciting [the mantra] sixty-four times. Then, reciting it thirty-two times, one should exhale the air through the right nostril. Again—

As before, having filled the air through the right nostril and performed *kumbhaka*, one should exhale the air through the left nostril. Again, as before, having filled the air through the left nostril and performed *kumbhaka*, one should exhale the air through the right nostril. If one is unable to do this, one should perform it by means of four recitations (*japa*).
Having filled the breath with air, one should perform *kumbhaka* (retention) by reciting [the mantra] sixteen times, and then exhale the air by reciting it eight times. This is *prāṇāyāma*.
Thereafter, one should perform *bhūtaśuddhi* (purification of the elements). Placing both hands palms-upward on one's lap and closing the eyes, [one should proceed] with the mantra.
Having united the individual soul (jīvātman), which is the wick-lamp of the heart, with Kuṇḍalinī residing in the Mūlādhāra,
and having caused it to pierce the six chakras known as Mūlādhāra, Svādhiṣṭhāna, Maṇipūra, Anāhata, Viśuddha, and Ājñā,
and having joined it there in Śiva within the thousand-petalled lotus at the head, [one should contemplate] earth, water, fire, and so forth right there.

Having contemplated that the twenty-four principles— consisting of air, ether, form, taste, smell, touch, sound, nose, tongue, eye, skin, ear, speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals, as well as primordial nature (prakṛti), mind (manas), intellect (buddhi), and ego (ahaṃkāra)— have dissolved, one becomes pure.
Having become composed of truth.
The sin resides in the left side of the belly, the size of a thumb;
it has the murder of a Brahmin for its head and the theft of gold for its two arms.
The heart of this body is the drinking of liquor, its two hips are the violation of the guru’s bed,
its pair of feet are the association with sin, and its hair is the minor offenses (upapātaka).
Having thus meditated upon the Person of Sin— wrathful, bearing a sword and shield, with faces turned downward, and unbearable— one should grasp the right nostril with the thumb of the right hand,
contemplate the seed-syllable *yaṃ* of air, which is smoke-colored, and recite it sixteen times through the left nostril.
Having filled [the body] with air and dried up the body together with the personification of sin (pāpapuruṣa), one should hold both nostrils,
contemplate the red-colored seed-syllable of fire "Raṃ," perform the breath-retention (kuṃbhaka),
and while reciting that [syllable] sixty-four times, one should burn the body along with the sin by means of the fire thus produced, [uttering] "Vaṃ."

Having visualized the seed-syllable of Varuṇa as white in color, one should wash away that heap of ashes with nectar consisting of the letters of the Mātṛkā, which flows from the moon on the forehead through thirty-two recitations of that [seed-syllable]. Then, exhaling the breath through the right nostril, one should contemplate oneself as the deity with the mantra "so 'haṃ."
Having contemplated the newly arisen body as water, and having contemplated the earth-born [element] as yellow in color,
one should visualize the body as very firm; then, with the twenty-four principles, one should contemplate the individual soul (jīvātman) and the Kuṇḍalinī.
"One should bring [the elements] together according to their respective places. This is the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*).
Then, one should perform the placement of the life-force (*jīvanyāsa*). Placing the hand on the heart with the *lelihāna* mudrā, [one recites]: "Oṃ Āṃ Hrīṃ Krīṃ Haṃ Saḥ!
The vital breaths (*prāṇa*) of the illustrious Dakṣiṇakālikā are here, the vital breaths are here! Oṃ Āṃ Hrīṃ Krīṃ Haṃ Saḥ.
The life-force of the glorious Dakṣiṇakālikā is situated here. ĀṂ HRĪṂ KRĪṂ HAṂ SAḤ;
all the sense organs of the glorious Dakṣiṇakālikā. Again, ĀṂ HRĪṂ KRĪṂ HAṂ SAḤ;
speech, mind, eyes, ears, nose, and breath of the glorious Dakṣiṇakālikā, having come here—
"May they remain happily for a long time, svāhā!"—thus is the placement of life-force (*jīvanyāsa*).
Then, with "oṃ āṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā," one should perform the purification of body, speech, and mind by means of the pervasive [mantra].
With "oṃ rakṣa (2) hūṃ phaṭ svāhā," one should place the hand upon the heart and perform self-protection.
Then one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the seer (*ṛṣi*) and so forth:
for this mantra of the venerable Dakṣiṇakālikā, Bhairava is the seer, Uṣṇik is the meter,
the venerable Dakṣiṇakālikā is the deity, *hrīṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *hūṃ* is the power (*śakti*), and *klīṃ* is the peg (*kīlaka*).
The application is for the sake of accomplishing the four aims of life: dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa.
Having recited this with palms joined in *añjali* and having offered water, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*):

"Salutation to Bhairava, the Seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to Uṣṇik, the Metre (*chandas*), in the mouth; salutation to the deity Śrī Dakṣiṇakālikā, in the heart; salutation to the seed-syllable *hrīṃ*, in the private parts; [salutation] to the feet."
HŪṂ, obeisance to Śakti. KLĪṂ, obeisance to the Kīlaka on all limbs. This is the application (viniyoga) for the attainment of the four aims of life: dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa.
Thereafter, one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the hands and the limbs.

Oṃ krīṃ, salutation to both thumbs. Oṃ krīṃ, salutation to both index fingers. Oṃ krūṃ, vaṣaṭ to both middle fingers. Oṃ kraiṃ, hūṃ to both ring fingers. Oṃ krauṃ, vauṣaṭ to both little fingers. Oṃ kraḥ, phaṭ to both palms and backs of the hands. Oṃ krīṃ.
*Hṛdayāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ krīṃ śirase svāhā*. *Oṃ krūṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*. *Oṃ kraiṃ kavacāya hūṃ*. *Oṃ krauṃ netratrayāya vauṣaṭ*. *Oṃ kraḥ astrāya phaṭ*.
Having uttered "phaṭ" and performed three upward claps (*tāla*), one should perform the binding of the ten directions (*digbandhana*) with snapping sounds (*chuṭikā*).
Then one should perform the deposition of the phonemes (*varṇanyāsa*).

*Am*, *āṃ*, *iṃ*, *īṃ*, *uṃ*, *ūṃ*, *ṛṃ*, *ṝṃ*, *ḷṃ*, *ḹṃ*, *namaḥ*—in the heart. In the right hand: *eṃ*, *aiṃ*, *oṃ*, *auṃ*, *aṃ*, *aḥṃ*, *kaṃ*, *khaṃ*, *gaṃ*, *ghaṃ*, *namaḥ*. In the left hand: *ṅaṃ*, *caṃ*, *chaṃ*.
*Jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ namaḥ* | On the right foot. *Ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ namaḥ* | On the left foot. *Maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ kṣaṃ namaḥ*.
Then one should perform the *mātṛkā-nyāsa*.

Of this venerable Mātṛkā-mantra, Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas), Mātṛkā Sarasvatī is the deity (devatā), the consonants are the seeds (bījas), the vowels are the powers (śaktis), the visarga is the bolt (kīlaka), and its application (viniyoga) is in the placement of the Mātṛkās. [One should place: "Salutation to Brahmā, the seer," on the head; "Salutation to Gāyatrī, the meter," on the mouth; [and] "on the heart" [one should place the deity].

Salutation to the deity Śrīmātṛkāsarasvatī; at the secret place (guhya). Salutation to the *hal* consonants, the seeds (*bīja*); at the two feet, salutation to the vowels, the powers (*śakti*). At all limbs, salutation to Garga, the wedge (*kīlaka*).
This is the application (*viniyoga*) in the Mātṛkā-nyāsa.

The *mātṛkā* and the ritual placement (*karāṅganyāsa*) are as follows: *Āṃ* to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*. *Iṃ* to the two index fingers, *svāhā*. *Uṃ* to the two middle fingers, *vaṣaṭ*. *Ṛṃ* to the two ring fingers, *huṃ*. *Ḷṃ* to the two little fingers, *vauṣaṭ*. *Eṃ* to the palms and backs of the hands, *phaṭ*. *Aiṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*. *Oṃ* to the head, *svāhā*. *Aum* to the tuft of hair (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*. *Auṃ* to the armor (*kavaca*), *huṃ*. *Aḥ* to the eyes, *vauṣaṭ*. *Kṣaṃ* to the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*. *Āṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ* to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*. *Iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ īṃ* to the two index fingers, *svāhā*. *Uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ* [to the two middle fingers, *vaṣaṭ*].

Ūṃ, *vaṣaṭ* to the two middle fingers; Eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ Aiṃ, *hūṃ* to the two ring fingers; Oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ Auṃ, *vauṣaṭ* to the two little fingers; Aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ Aḥ.
*Phaṭ* with both palms and the backs of the hands. *Aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ*, homage to the heart (*hṛdayāya namaḥ*).
*Iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ īṃ*, *svāhā* to the head (*śirase svāhā*).
*Uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ Ūṃ*, *vaṣaṭ* to the crest-lock (*śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*). *Eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ*.
Naṃ Aiṃ Kavacāya Hūṃ. Oṃ Paṃ Phaṃ Baṃ Bhaṃ Maṃ Auṃ Netratrayāya Vauṣaṭ. Aṃ Yaṃ Raṃ Laṃ Vaṃ Śaṃ Ṣaṃ Saṃ Haṃ Laṃ Kṣaṃ Aṃḥ Astrāya Phaṭ.
Now, the meditation on the internal *mātṛkā*:
[one should meditate upon her] who consists of the letters from *A* to *Kṣa*, possessing the luster of fresh dawn, seated upon the petals of six lotuses,
endowed with three blue-lotus eyes, having a face like the full moon, and equal to the essence of nectar.

One should meditate upon the Mistress of the Sun (Taraṇeśvarī), who wears a crown of five locks, who is languid from the weight of her breasts, and who holds a crescent moon, a deer, and a book on her forehead;
having thus meditated and worshipped her with mental offerings, one should perform the internal placement of the Mātṛkās at the throat.

In the sixteen-petaled Viśuddha-cakra: aṃ namaḥ, āṃ namaḥ, iṃ namaḥ, īṃ namaḥ, uṃ namaḥ, ūṃ namaḥ, ṛṃ namaḥ, ṝṃ namaḥ, ḷṃ namaḥ, ḹṃ namaḥ, eṃ namaḥ, aiṃ namaḥ, oṃ namaḥ, auṃ namaḥ, aṃ namaḥ, aḥ namaḥ. In the heart, at the Anāhata-cakra.

At the twelve-petaled [lotus] in the throat: *kaṃ namaḥ*, *khaṃ namaḥ*, *gaṃ namaḥ*, *ghaṃ namaḥ*, *ṅaṃ namaḥ*, *caṃ namaḥ*, *chaṃ namaḥ*, *jaṃ namaḥ*, *jhaṃ namaḥ*, *ñaṃ namaḥ*, *ṭaṃ namaḥ*, *ṭhaṃ namaḥ*. At the ten-petaled Maṇipūra-cakra in the navel: *ḍaṃ namaḥ*, *ḍhaṃ namaḥ*, *ṇaṃ namaḥ*.

To that [Ta] obeisance; to Tha obeisance; to Da obeisance; to Dha obeisance; to Na obeisance; to Pa obeisance; to Pha obeisance. In the Svādhiṣṭhāna-cakra at the liṅga, which has six petals: to Ba obeisance; to Bha obeisance; to Ma obeisance; to Ya obeisance; to Ra obeisance; to La obeisance.
In the four-petalled *mūlādhāra*, [worship] with *vaṃ namaḥ*, *śaṃ namaḥ*, *ṣaṃ namaḥ*, and *saṃ namaḥ*.

In the two-petalled *ājñācakra* between the eyebrows, [worship] with *haṃ namaḥ* and *kṣaṃ namaḥ*. Within the triangle (*trikoṇa*) beginning with *a*, *ka*, and *tha*, situated at the pericarp of the thousand-petalled lotus located at the head, [begin] from the left line...

Moving clockwise: aṃ namaḥ, āṃ namaḥ, iṃ namaḥ, īṃ namaḥ, uṃ namaḥ, ūṃ namaḥ, ṛṃ namaḥ, ṝṃ namaḥ, ḷṃ namaḥ, ḹṃ namaḥ, eṃ namaḥ, aiṃ namaḥ, oṃ namaḥ, auṃ namaḥ, aṃ namaḥ, aḥ namaḥ. On the upward line: kaṃ namaḥ, khaṃ [namaḥ].
Homage to Gaṃ; homage to Ghaṃ; homage to Ṅaṃ; homage to Caṃ; homage to Chaṃ; homage to Jaṃ;
homage to Jhaṃ; homage to Ñaṃ; homage to Ṭaṃ; homage to Ṭhaṃ; homage to Ḍaṃ; homage to Ḍhaṃ; homage to Ṇaṃ; homage to Taṃ;
homage to Thaṃ; homage to Daṃ; homage to Dhaṃ; homage to Naṃ.
Namaḥ paṃ, namaḥ phaṃ, namaḥ baṃ, namaḥ bhaṃ, namaḥ maṃ, namaḥ yaṃ, namaḥ raṃ, namaḥ laṃ, namaḥ vaṃ, namaḥ śaṃ, namaḥ ṣaṃ, namaḥ saṃ.
In the lower corner: haṃ namaḥ; in the left corner: laṃ namaḥ; in the right corner: kṣaṃ namaḥ.
In the center of that is the supreme bindu, which consists of emanation and dissolution;
with that divine nectar, one should satisfy the Supreme Goddess.
Thus, with a concentrated mind, one should meditate; this is another form of *nyāsa*. Now follows the meditation on the external emanation of the *mātṛkā*:
[one should visualize her] whose face, belly, arms, and thighs are divided by the fifty letters.

I take refuge in the Goddess of Speech, who possesses three eyes and radiant luster; she rests upon the head of the Effulgent One (Śiva), whose crown is adorned with the crescent moon; she holds in her lotus-like hands a mudrā, a rosary, and a jar brimming with nectar; and her full, lofty breasts are beautifully swelling.
Having meditated thus and worshipped with mental offerings, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) on the forehead,

the face-circle, the two eyes (right and left), the two ears, the two nostrils, the two cheeks, the upper and lower lips, the upper and lower rows of teeth, the *brahmarandhra*, and the tongue, [uttering]: *aṃ* namaḥ, *āṃ* [namaḥ].

*Namaḥ* iṃ, *namaḥ* īṃ, *namaḥ* uṃ, *namaḥ* ūṃ, *namaḥ* ṛṃ, *namaḥ* ṝṃ, *namaḥ* ḷṃ, *namaḥ* ḹṃ, *namaḥ* eṃ, *namaḥ* aiṃ, *namaḥ* oṃ, *namaḥ* auṃ, *namaḥ* aṃ, *namaḥ* aḥ. [These are placed] on the root of the right upper arm, the elbow, the wrist, and at the roots and tips of the fingers. *Caṃ* *namaḥ*.

*Chaṃ* namaḥ, *jaṃ* namaḥ, *jhaṃ* namaḥ, *ñaṃ* namaḥ— at the root of the right thigh, the joint of the knee, the ankle, and the base and tip of the toes. *Ṭaṃ* namaḥ, *ṭhaṃ* namaḥ, *ḍaṃ* namaḥ, *ḍhaṃ* namaḥ, *ṇaṃ* namaḥ.
On the root of the left thigh, the joint of the knee, the ankle, and the base and tips of the toes: *taṃ namaḥ*, *thaṃ namaḥ*, *daṃ namaḥ*, *dhaṃ namaḥ*, *naṃ namaḥ*.
On the right and left sides: *paṃ namaḥ*, *phaṃ namaḥ*. On the back: *vaṃ namaḥ*. At the navel: *bhaṃ namaḥ*.

*Bhaṃ* namaḥ to the belly; *maṃ* namaḥ to the heart; *yaṃ* *namaḥ* to the skin-self (*tvagātman*); *raṃ* *namaḥ* to the blood-self (*asṛgātman*) on the right shoulder; *laṃ* *namaḥ* to the flesh-self (*māṃsātman*) on the back of the neck (*kakud*); *vaṃ* *namaḥ* to the fat-self (*meda-ātman*) on the left shoulder; *śaṃ* *namaḥ* to the bone-self (*asthyātman*) from the heart to the right hand. [From the heart]...

In the left hand: *ṣaṃ*, salutation to the self of marrow (*majjātmane namaḥ*). From the heart to the right foot: *saṃ*, salutation to the self of semen (*śukrātmane namaḥ*). From the heart to the left foot: *haṃ*, salutation to the self of life-force (*jīvātmane namaḥ*). From the heart to the abdomen: *laṃ*, salutation to the self of breath (*prāṇātmane namaḥ*). From the heart to the mouth: *kṣaṃ*, salutation to the supreme self (*paramātmane namaḥ*). Thus.
The Sṛṣṭinyāsa. Now, the meditation on the Mātṛkā of the State (sthiti):
[He who is] of the luster of vermilion, adorned with immeasurable ornaments, and three-eyed.
One should meditate on [the deity] holding a rosary of knowledge, a deer cub, and a choice fruit,
with the Blessed Lady standing at his side, her body golden-hued, holding a book and a rosary of beads in her lotus-like hands.

Having meditated thus and worshipped with mental offerings, one should place the letters from *ḍa* to *va* in the locations of the Mātṛkā, starting from the right ankle and ending at the right knee, as follows: at the right ankle, *ḍaṃ namaḥ*; at the base and tip of its toes...
Ḍhaṃ namaḥ, ṇaṃ namaḥ—on the left thigh, the joint of the knee, the ankle, and the roots and tips of the toes of the feet;
taṃ namaḥ, thaṃ namaḥ, daṃ namaḥ, dhaṃ namaḥ, naṃ namaḥ—on the right and left sides; paṃ namaḥ, phaṃ namaḥ—on the back; vaṃ namaḥ.
At the navel and the belly: *bhaṃ* namaḥ, *maṃ* namaḥ. At the heart: *tvagātmane namaḥ*.

On the right shoulder: *raṃ* asṛgātmane namaḥ. At the crown of the head: *laṃ* māṃsātmane namaḥ. On the left shoulder: *vaṃ* medaātmane namaḥ. From the heart to the right hand: *śaṃ* asthyātmane [namaḥ].
Salutation! From the heart and so forth, on the left hand: *ṣaṃ* to the self of marrow, salutation! From the heart and so forth, on the right foot:
*śaṃ* to the self of semen, salutation! From the heart and so forth, on the left foot: *haṃ* to the self of life-force (*jīva*), salutation! From the heart and so forth, in the abdomen:
*laṃ* to the self of breath (*prāṇa*), salutation! From the heart and so forth, in the mouth: *kṣaṃ* to the supreme self (*paramātman*), salutation!
On the forehead, the face-circle, the right and left eyes, as well as the two ears, the two nostrils, the two cheeks, the upper and lower lips,
the upper and lower rows of teeth, the *brahmarandhra*, and the tongue: *aṃ namaḥ*, *āṃ namaḥ*, *iṃ namaḥ*, *īṃ namaḥ*, *uṃ namaḥ*, *ūṃ namaḥ*, *ṛṃ namaḥ*, *ṝṃ namaḥ*, *ḷṃ* [namaḥ].

*Namaḥ* *ḷṃ*, *namaḥ* *eṃ*, *namaḥ* *aiṃ*, *namaḥ* *oṃ*, *namaḥ* *auṃ*, *namaḥ* *aṃ*, *namaḥ* *aḥ*— to the roots of the right upper arm, the elbow, the wrist, the base of the fingers, and the tips of the fingers. *Kaṃ namaḥ*, *khaṃ namaḥ*, *gaṃ namaḥ*, *ghaṃ namaḥ*, *ṅaṃ namaḥ*.
On the root of the left upper arm, the elbow, the wrist, and at the roots and tips of the fingers of the hand:
*caṃ* namaḥ, *chaṃ* namaḥ, *jaṃ* namaḥ, *jhaṃ* namaḥ, *ñaṃ* namaḥ.
On the root of the right thigh and the knee: *ṭaṃ* namaḥ, *ṭhaṃ* namaḥ. Thus ends the placement of the stationary Mātṛkā (*sthitimātṛkānyāsa*).
Now, the meditation on the Saṃhāramātṛkā:
[One should meditate upon her] as three-eyed, incessantly holding in her hands a rosary, a young deer, a lofty axe, and a lore (vidyā).
Bow down to the Mistress of Speech, who bears the crescent moon upon her head, whose complexion is like a red lotus,
and who is bent by the weight of her breasts.
Having meditated thus and worshipped with mental offerings, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*).
One should place the letters from *kṣa* down to *a* in the locations starting from the mouth and ending at the forehead, as follows:
*kṣaṃ* to the Supreme Self (*paramātman*) on the heart and the mouth; *laṃ* to the Self of Vital Breath (*prāṇātman*) on the heart and the stomach.

*Namaḥ*. From the heart to the left foot: *haṃ*, obeisance to the self of life-force (*jīvātman*). From the heart to the right foot: *saṃ*, obeisance to the self of semen (*śukrātman*). From the heart to the left hand: *ṣaṃ*, obeisance to the self of marrow (*majjātman*). From the heart to the right hand: *śaṃ*, obeisance to the self of bone (*asthyātman*). On the left shoulder: *vaṃ*, obeisance to the self of fat (*medātman*).

Kakudi (the crown of the head): *laṃ*, obeisance to the self consisting of flesh. On the right shoulder: *raṃ*, obeisance to the self consisting of blood. At the heart: *tvagātmane namaḥ* (obeisance to the self consisting of skin). In the belly, navel, back, left side, and right side: *maṃ namaḥ*, *bhaṃ namaḥ*, *vaṃ namaḥ*, *phaṃ namaḥ*, *paṃ namaḥ*.
On the tips, bases, ankles, and knee-joints of the left foot, and on the root of the thigh: *naṃ namaḥ*, *dhaṃ namaḥ*, *daṃ namaḥ*, *thaṃ namaḥ*, *taṃ namaḥ*.
[Likewise] on the tips, bases, ankles, and knee-joints of the right foot...
At the roots of the thighs: *ṇaṃ namaḥ*, *ḍhaṃ namaḥ*, *ḍaṃ namaḥ*, *ṭhaṃ namaḥ*, *ṭaṃ namaḥ*.
At the tips of the fingers, the bases of the fingers, the wrists, and the roots of the arms of the left hand: *ñaṃ namaḥ*, *jhaṃ namaḥ*, *jaṃ namaḥ*, *chaṃ namaḥ*, *caṃ namaḥ*.
Upon the tips of the fingers of the right hand, at the base of the fingers, the wrist, the elbow, and the root of the upper arm:

*ṅaṃ namaḥ*, *ghaṃ namaḥ*, *gaṃ namaḥ*, *khaṃ namaḥ*, *kaṃ namaḥ*. [Then] upon the tongue, the *brahmarandhra*, the lower and upper rows of teeth, the lower lip, the left and right cheeks, and likewise the two nostrils.

On the two ears, the two eyes, the face, the circle [of the forehead], and the forehead: *aḥ* namaḥ, *aṃ* namaḥ, *auṃ* namaḥ, *oṃ* namaḥ, *aiṃ* namaḥ, *eṃ* namaḥ, *ḹṃ* namaḥ, *ḷṃ* namaḥ, *ṝṃ* namaḥ, *ṛṃ* namaḥ, *ūṃ* namaḥ, *uṃ* namaḥ, *īṃ* namaḥ, *iṃ* namaḥ, *āṃ* namaḥ, *aṃ* namaḥ. Thus.
The ritual placement (nyāsa) of the Saṃhāra-mātṛkā.

Furthermore, the householder should perform the nyāsa of creation (sṛṣṭi) and maintenance (sthiti). In another tantra, the nyāsa of the Mātṛkās is said to be fivefold: creation, maintenance, withdrawal (saṃhṛti), and then again creation and maintenance; thus it is remembered as being of five kinds. This is also stated in the Gautamīya.
The withdrawal (saṃhṛti) is proclaimed as that which removes the collection of defects;
and at the end of creation, it bestows knowledge upon those of pure mind who abide in the stages of life (varṇin).

For householders, there are three stages ending with maintenance; for those who desire [results], they follow their inclinations. Some maintain that for the forest-dweller whose fire is innate (sahajagni), there is only the stage of maintenance.

For the sages and for one who is entirely dispassionate, the three types of renunciation (nyāsa) should always be performed until the end of their dissolution; however, for one who is incapable, only one [type] should indeed be performed.
However, some [teachers] maintain that one should perform the placement (nyāsa) in five ways or even in three ways among all the castes and stages of life (varṇāśrama).

In this context, for worship intended for specific desires (kāmya) and so forth, the placement of the Śrīkaṇṭha-mātṛkā is prescribed; the two types of sixfold placement (ṣoḍhānyāsa) should also be performed, but they are not written here for fear of excessive length.
Now, the sixfold placement of the general seed-syllables (*sāmānyabīja-ṣoḍhānyāsa*).

As follows: *Oṃ namaḥ* on the head; *Oṃ hrīṃ strīṃ hūṃ phaṭ namaḥ* on the space between the eyebrows; *Eṃ namaḥ* on the throat; *Klīṃ namaḥ* on the heart; *Aiṃ namaḥ* on the navel; *Klīṃ namaḥ* on the genitals; *Sauṃ* on the secret place.
*Namaḥ*. *Hūṃ namaḥ* on the right hand; *Śrīṃ namaḥ* on the left hand; *Hrīṃ namaḥ* on the right foot;

*Klīṃ namaḥ* on the left foot; *Krīṃ namaḥ* on the back. Thus, thereafter, the *tattvanyāsa* and *bījanyāsa* should be performed upon the entire *vidyā*, as follows: from the navel up to the heart on the right.

In the *kālika* [rite]: *oṃṃ vidyā-tattvāya namaḥ*. From the heart up to the *brahmarandhra*, one should perform: *krīṃ krīṃ krīṃ hūṃ hūṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ*. *Krīṃ namaḥ* at the *brahmarandhra*; *krīṃ namaḥ* between the eyebrows;
*krīṃ namaḥ* on the forehead; *hūṃ namaḥ* at the navel; *hūṃ namaḥ* at the secret place; *hrīṃ namaḥ* at the mouth.
"Hrīṃ, salutation to all limbs. Thus is the seed-syllable placement (bījanyāsa).

Then, with the root mantra, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) seven times from the head down to the feet and from the feet up to the head; likewise seven times from the mouth down to the belly and from the belly up to the mouth, using both hands separately.

Then, one should recite the seven-leaved [lotus] seven times with the mantra *oṃ hrīṃ mūlaṃ hrīṃ*. Thereafter, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the pedestal (*pīṭha*). At the pericarp of the heart-lotus: *oṃ ādhāraśaktaye namaḥ*; *oṃ prakṛtyai namaḥ*.
Likewise, [one should place them] for Kamaṭha, Śeṣa, the Earth, the Ocean of Nectar, and Maṇidvīpa.

To the cremation ground that is a house of wish-fulfilling gems, and to the *pārijāta* tree at its base: *Oṃ*, salutation to the jeweled altar (*ratnavedikā*). Upon it: *Oṃ*, salutation to the gem-studded pedestal (*maṇipīṭha*). In the four directions: *Oṃ*, salutation to the sages (*munayaḥ*). Likewise, salutation to the gods (*devāḥ*). Salutation to the corpses and skulls (*śavamuṇḍāni*). On the right shoulder: *Oṃ*, salutation to Dharma (*dharmaḥ*).
On the left shoulder: *oṃ jñānāya namaḥ*. On the left thigh: *oṃ vairāgyāya namaḥ*. On the right side:
*oṃ anaiśvaryāya namaḥ*. In all cases, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) beginning with the syllable *praṇava* (*oṃ*) and ending with *namaḥ*.
Again, on the pericarp (*karṇikā*): *aṃ anaṃtāya namaḥ*. *paṃ padmāya namaḥ*. *āṃ*.

ĀṂ, salutation to Ānanda; SAṂ, salutation to the consciousness-stalk (saṃvinnālā); PAṂ, salutation to the petals consisting of Prakṛti; VIṂ, salutation to the filaments consisting of the transformations (vikāra); TAṂ, salutation to the pericarp whose form is the Tattvas;
AṂ, salutation to the solar orb (arkamaṇḍala) consisting of twelve kalās.

Oṃ, obeisance to the lunar maṇḍala, whose self consists of sixteen digits. Maṃ, obeisance to the fire maṇḍala, whose self consists of ten digits. Saṃ, obeisance to sattva. Raṃ, obeisance to rajas. Taṃ, obeisance to tamas. Āṃ, obeisance to the Self (Ātman). Aṃ, obeisance to the Inner Self (Antarātman). Paṃ, obeisance to the Supreme Self (Paramātman).
*Hrīṃ*, salutation to the Self of Knowledge (*jñānātmane*).
Then, one should install the powers of the seat (*pīṭhaśakti*) upon the filaments of the heart-lotus, starting from the east and proceeding clockwise:
*Oṃ*, salutation to Will (*icchā*); *Oṃ*, salutation to Knowledge (*jñānā*); *Oṃ*, salutation to Action (*kriyā*); *Oṃ*, salutation to Kāminī.
Salutation! Oṃ, salutation to Kāmadāyinī; Oṃ, salutation to Rati; Oṃ, salutation to Ratipriyā;

Oṃ, salutation to Ānandā. In the center, Maṃ, salutation to Manonmanī. Above that, Aiṃ, salutation to Parā, Aparā, and Parāparā; Hsauḥ, salutation to Sadāśiva, the great corpse-seat upon the lotus throne. Thus.
The ritual placement of the seats (pīṭhanyāsa).

Then, having performed breath control (prāṇāyāma) and the six-limbed ritual placement (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa), one should meditate upon the Goddess. The meditation is as follows: [one should meditate on] Kālikā, the Divine Dakṣiṇā, who has a terrifying face, is formidable, has loose hair, possesses four arms, and is adorned with a garland of severed heads.
Her left upper and lower lotus-hands hold a sword with its blade recently severed,
while her right upper and lower hands grant the gestures of fearlessness and the boon.
She has the luster of a great cloud, is dark-complexioned, and likewise naked;
she has a garland of severed heads hanging from her neck, smeared with trickling blood.
She had brought the ears of the virtuous to serve as her earrings, was terrifying with a pair of skulls,
possessed formidable fangs and a gaping mouth, and had full, elevated breasts.
Her limbs are adorned with every ornament, she is the destroyer of all that is inauspicious;
she wears a girdle made from the gathered hands of corpses, her face is smiling.
Her face is made radiant by streams of blood trickling from both corners of her mouth;
she utters a terrible roar, is exceedingly fierce, and dwells in the cremation ground.
She possesses three eyes shaped like the orb of the rising sun;
she is formidable, with a necklace of pearls hanging down that extends across her right side.
O Mahādeva in the form of a Śava, she is seated upon your heart and surrounded on all four sides by Śivās of terrible roar.
Her eyes rolling from wine, her tongue lolling, and laughing with loud bursts of laughter,
she was intoxicated and engaged in the inverted act together with Mahākāla.
Her eyes were bright with happiness, and her lotus-like face was smiling.
One should thus meditate upon Kālī, who grants dharma, desire, wealth, and liberation, her body adorned with a serpent as a sacred thread and her crest fashioned from the crescent moon.
Immediately after the meditations, as follows:
[one should visualize] the Goddess, resembling a mountain of collyrium, the auspicious Śivā with a formidable face,
beautiful, adorned with a garland of severed heads, with disheveled hair and a smiling countenance.
[He saw her] seated upon the lotus-heart of Mahākāla, with yellow breasts,
intent on inverted sexual union, possessing terrible fangs, and together with the Śivas.
She has a serpent as her sacred thread, with the crescent moon as her crest-jewel;
she is endowed with all ornaments and adorned with pearls and gems.
She was girdled with thousands of dead hands, naked,
and resplendent with millions of Yoginīs who were like millions of Śivās.
Her lotus-face drinks blood, she is intoxicated by drinking wine,
her eyes are fire, sun, and moon, and her face quivers with redness.
She had earrings made from the ears of two young horses that had been severed;
a garland of severed heads hung from her neck, stained with trickling blood.
[One should meditate on her] in the cremation ground, standing in the midst of fire, saluted by Brahmā and Keśava,
with a freshly severed head [as an ornament], and with lotus-hands displaying the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.
As for the intermediate dhyāna (*dhyānāntara*):
it resembles split collyrium, appearing like a corpse that has been cut open,
with a smiling lotus-face from which streams of blood are flowing.
She possessed a pair of full and elevated breasts, a broad chest, and ample hips;
she was the southern direction, with disheveled hair, delighting the naked quarters.
Mahākāla, who is mounted upon a corpse, abides in the midst of a smiling bliss,
and is resplendent with yoginīs whose faces and eyes are deep red.
Her shoulders are adorned with two corpses, she is radiant with a tilaka-mark of vermilion,
and she wears a garland made of fifty severed heads, crimson with blood.
Abounding in the splendor of various jewels, adorned with diverse ornaments,
having a bracelet fashioned from human bone, and decorated with conch-shell bangles;
In one place, she was seated upon the chest of a corpse, licking at it;
in another, she had taken a mouthful of the flesh of a corpse and was laughing with loud, repeated bursts of laughter.
She holds a sword and a severed head in her left hands, while bestowing fearlessness and granting boons with her right;
she is tusked, exceedingly fierce, and most terrifying with her violent roar.
She was surrounded by auspicious jackals howling with terrible cries, the destroyer of fear, who spoke with fearsome sounds, saying, "Do not fear! Do not fear! to her own devotees.
To her who spoke thus, "What boon do you desire? I shall grant it," [he replied:]
The intermediate dhyāna.
She holds in her hands a freshly severed sword and the gesture of fearlessness; she has a terrible face and wears a beautiful garland of heads with loose, flowing tresses of hair;
from the corners of her mouth flows blood, and she is adorned with the dust of the cremation ground and the entrails of corpses.
I worship the goddess Kālikā, whose dark limbs are adorned with a girdle made of human hands.
The intermediate dhyāna.

She has a body like a cloud, is naked, and is mounted upon a corpse and a jackal; she is the supreme goddess with three eyes, terrifying with a pair of arrows hanging down to her ears, and wearing a garland of severed heads.
In her lower left lotus-hand she holds a human head, and in the other [right] hand a sword.
I always worship Kālikā, who possesses a mass of loosened hair that bestows fearlessness through her generosity.
Having meditated upon one of these and placed a flower upon one's own head, one should worship with mental offerings as follows:
one should offer a seat in the heart-lotus with the nectar flowing from the thousand-spoked [cakra] of Acyuta.
One should offer water for the feet at the feet and present the mind as the arghya offering.
One should offer that water for rinsing the mouth into a golden vessel;
one should offer the honey-mixture (madhuparka) into the mouth, and again the water for rinsing the mouth.
With that nectar, one should also prepare a bath for all the limbs,
as well as a garment of the principle of space (ākāśatattva) and various ornaments.
The wise one, according to the reality of the twenty-four [tattvas], should offer fragrance,
as well as self-arisen flowers, saffron, and red sandalwood.
One should mentally fashion the flower and apply the incense to the vital breaths;
the lamp is the principle of fire (tejas-tattva), and the food offering is an ocean of nectar.
One should offer meat and pork, a mountain of fried fish,
heaps of beans with rice, and side dishes smeared with ghee.
Deep red sacrificial porridge (caru), supreme cooked rice smeared with ghee,
an ocean of curd and milk, and various roots and fruits.
Food to be chewed, food to be swallowed, as well as that to be licked, drunk, and masticated— the supreme nectar and the drinking water,
well-scented with the flowers of one’s inner disposition;
and that flower which is the nectar of the *kula*, not merely water cleansed by the *kuta*.
Having again offered water for sipping (ācamana), one should present betel-leaf (tāmbūla).

Having offered an oblation to desire and anger, which act as obstacles, one should perform the recitation (*japa*). Regarding the rosary of letters: one should visualize the rosary consisting of the letters from *a* to *kṣa*, composed of phonemes, joined with the *bindu*, strung upon the thread of the nature of Śiva and Śakti, and marked by the knots of Kuṇḍalinī.

One should recite: *aṃ mūlaṃ*, *āṃ mūlaṃ*, and so forth. Having recited the mantra after each letter up to the end of the letters ending in *la*, one should utter the letter *kṣa* alone, which is in the form of Mount Meru, and then recite the mantra once for each of the final letters. Thus, having recited the mantra one hundred and eight times, one should offer it with this: *oṃ*.

"O Mother Kālī, first of all, who dwells in the innermost self of all, whose nature is the internal light, accept this internal recitation; salutations to you! Having thus offered the recitation, one should prostrate.

Now, as for the internal oblation (*antarhoma*): having visualized oneself as undivided, one should contemplate the square fire-pit of consciousness (*cit-kuṇḍa*), whose nature is the Self, the Inner Self, the Supreme Self, and the Knowledge-Self;
which is beautiful with the girdle of bliss, marked by the three folds of the *bindu*, and has the form of the womb (*yoni*) consisting of the half-measure (*ardhamātra*).

Having visualized the *cit-kuṇḍa* (the fire-pit of consciousness) at the navel, one should offer oblations there into the fire of pure awareness (*saṃvidagni*). Reciting the root mantra: "I, whose mental activity is constant, perpetually offer [myself] as an oblation with the ladle of the mind into the fire whose form is the consciousness of the navel, which is kindled by knowledge—*svāhā*. This is the first oblation.
Having recited the root mantra:

"With the mind as the sacrificial ladle, I perpetually offer the fluctuations of the senses as oblations into the blazing fire of the Self, which is kindled by dharma and adharma, via the path of the suṣumnā."
"SVĀHĀ"—this is the second oblation. Having recited the root mantra:
"With the hands of light and space, grasping the *unmanī* ladle, I offer into the fire that which is filled with the oil of the digits of merit and demerit."

*Svāhā!* Thus is the third oblation. Having recited the root mantra: "In the fire of consciousness, which blazes within without fuel and incessantly, which is the adversary to the blinding darkness, and which is the ground for the unfolding of certain wondrous rays—I offer into it the entire universe, from the earth up to Śiva."

" Svāhā!"— thus is the fourth full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*). Then, having praised the bed which resembles the ocean of milk, one should settle the Goddess there together with Mahākāla and satisfy the Blessed Lady with various songs, instrumental music, dances, and so forth, produced from the essence of aesthetic sentiments (*rasa*) such as the erotic (*śṛṅgāra*).

"One should prostrate"—this refers to the mental sacrifice (*mānasayāga*). Thereafter, one should begin the external worship (*bāhyapūjā*). In that regard, first one should perform the installation of the *arghya* (offering water). Having drawn a mandala consisting of a triangle, a circle, and a square on one's left, one should consecrate the mandala with the mantra "phaṭ."

"Oṃ, these perfumes and flowers; Hrīṃ, obeisance to the Support-Power (Ādhāraśakti). Having thus worshipped the mandala, [one says] "Phaṭ, obeisance to the seat consisting of the three-legged stand and so forth," and having washed it, [one says] "Namaḥ," and places it upon the mandala.
[One says] "Maṃ, obeisance to the Fire-mandala consisting of ten digits (kalās)," and having thus worshipped the support (ādhāra), [one says] "Phaṭ."

Having washed the vessel, such as a conch, and placed it there with "Namaḥ," one should worship the *arghya* vessel with "Aṃ, obeisance to the solar orb consisting of twelve digits" (*namaḥ*). Then, having filled it with water and "Namaḥ," and having cast some *kāraṇa* [substance] into it, one recites "Oṃ."

"Obeisance to the lunar maṇḍala, whose self consists of sixteen digits. Having thus worshipped the nectar of the *arghya*, one should invoke the sacred waters (*tīrthas*) there with the mantra beginning "Oṃ Gaṅge... while employing the *aṅkuśa-mudrā*. [One should offer] red flowers and the like, bilva leaves, *dūrvā* grass, unbroken rice (*akṣata*), white and red sandalwood, pure fish, water, and *kula* flowers.

Having cast [the vessel] therein and invoked the Goddess with "Hūṃ," one should veil her with "Avaguṇṭhaya. Having rendered her nectarine with the *dhenu-mudrā* using "Vaṃ" and the root mantra, one should inflame her with the *yoni-mudrā*. Displaying the *śaṅkha-mudrā* with "Oṃ," one should effect the ritual integration (*sakalīkaraṇa*) with the six limb-mantras and cover her with the *matsya-mudrā*. Therein...
Having recited the root mantra ten times and visualized the arghya as having the form of the Goddess,

one should worship the Goddess there with perfumes, flowers, incense, and lamps; until the conclusion of the worship, one must not move the arghya vessel— this is the ritual for establishing the arghya.
There, having placed one *prokṣaṇī* vessel just as one does for the general *arghya*,

and having poured a little water from the *arghya* vessel into that *prokṣaṇī* vessel, one should sprinkle oneself and the articles of worship with that water, and [place them] before one on the lion-throne or similar seat.

One should install either an image or a yantra. As for the yantra: it should be drawn with a golden needle upon a vessel made of gold, silver, copper, wood from a cremation ground, or sandalwood from a sacrificial tree, or even on a human skull; the vessel should be smeared with self-arisen flowers, kuṇḍagolaka, red sandalwood, and so forth.
Alternatively, with a *bilva* thorn, one should draw a downward-facing triangle, surrounded by a circle;
outside that, an eight-petalled lotus, surrounded by a circle; and outside that, a square enclosure (*bhūpura*) provided with four gates, with a *bindu-cakra* in the center.
To the left of the *bindu-cakra* is the seed-syllable *klīṃ*, and to the right is the seed-syllable *hrīṃ*. Thus.

One should draw the yantra. Alternatively, one should worship it in a non-earthen Śiva-liṅga made of crystal or other materials, or in an installed yantra, or in a yantra made of flowers and so forth. Having thus established either the yantra or the image, one should perform the worship of the pedestal (pīṭhapūjā) there, as follows: at the pericarp (karṇikā), "Oṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti. Oṃ...

Salutation to Prakṛti. Likewise [salutation] to Kamaṭha, to Śeṣa, to the Earth, to the Ocean of Nectar, to Maṇidvīpa, to the House of the Cintāmaṇi jewel, to the cremation ground, to the Pārijāta tree, and at its base to the jeweled altar (ratnavedikā). Oṃ, salutation to the jeweled pedestal; salutation to the sages in the four directions; Oṃ, salutation to the Vedas.

Oṃ, salutation to the corpse, the skull, the funeral pyre, the charcoal, and the bone. Salutation to the jackals, who are intoxicated by the abundance of flesh and bones. [Offerings] to Dharma, Jñāna, Vairāgya, and Aiśvarya in the four corners starting from the southeast in clockwise order; and to the four directions starting from the east.

For Adharma, for Ignorance (Ajñāna), for Non-detachment (Avairāgya), and for Lack of Sovereignty (Anaiśvarya), one should worship everywhere with the *praṇava* at the beginning and *namaḥ* at the end. Again, in the pericarp (*karṇikā*): *aṃ* to Ananta, *namaḥ*; *paṃ* to the Lotus (*padma*), *namaḥ*; *āṃ* to the Root of Bliss (*ānandakanda*), *namaḥ*; *saṃ* to the Consciousness-stalk (*savit-nāla*), *namaḥ*; *praṃ* to the petals consisting of Prakṛti, *namaḥ*.

Oṃ Namaḥ! Homage to the filaments consisting of the transformation of *biṃ*. Homage to the pericarp whose nature is the *tat* syllable. Homage to the solar orb (*arka-maṇḍala*) consisting of twelve digits (*kalā*), Oṃ. Homage to the lunar orb (*soma-maṇḍala*) consisting of sixteen digits, Uṃ. Homage to the fire orb (*vahni-maṇḍala*), Maṃ.
Salutation to the one whose self consists of the ten digits (*daśakalātman*). Salutation to *saṃ* for *sattva*. Salutation to *raṃ* for *rajas*. Salutation to *taṃ* for *tamas*.

Salutation to *āṃ* for the *ātman*. Salutation to *aṃ* for the *antarātman*. Salutation to *paṃ* for the *paramātman*. Salutation to *hrīṃ* for the *jñānātman*. [One should worship] the powers of the seat (*pīṭhaśakti*) upon the filaments, starting from the east and proceeding clockwise.
One should worship: Oṃ, salutation to Icchā; Oṃ, salutation to Kāmadāyinī; Oṃ, salutation to Rati; Oṃ, salutation to Ratipriyā;
Oṃ, salutation to Ānandā. In the center, [worship] Maṃ, salutation to Manonmanī.
Above that: *aiṃ* obeisance to Parā; *aparāyai parāparāyai* *hsauṃ* obeisance to Sadāśiva, the great preta-lotus seat. Thus is the worship of the seat (*pīṭhapūjā*).

In this context, during the worship of the special secret (*viśeṣarahasya-pūjā*), one should perform the purification of the five principles (*pañcatattva*) beginning with the *kāraṇa* [vessel]. Now, the installation of the *kāraṇa-kumbha* is as follows: first, having established one’s own consort (*svīya-śakti*) endowed with auspicious marks to one’s left, then, to one’s left...

On the ground to the right of the Goddess, having drawn a mandala consisting of a dot, a hexagon, and a square, [one says] "Phaṭ" and thus consecrates the mandala with sprinkling. Saying "Hrīṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti," one worships the mandala with "Phaṭ" and thus consecrates the support with sprinkling.
Then, saying "Namaḥ," one places it upon the mandala.

"Oṃ maṃ, obeisance to the fire-maṇḍala consisting of ten kalās. Having thus worshipped the support (ādhāra), [he says] "phaṭ," and having washed the pitcher (kuṃbha), [he says] "namaḥ," and having placed it there, he adorns the pitcher with red cloth, garlands, vermilion, and so forth. [He then says: "Aṃ, obeisance to the sun-maṇḍala."
"Obeisance to the one whose self consists of twelve digits. Having thus worshipped the water-pot (kalaśa), [one recites]:
*kṣaṃ laṃ haṃ saṃ ṣaṃ śaṃ vaṃ laṃ raṃ yaṃ maṃ bhaṃ baṃ phaṃ paṃ naṃ dhaṃ daṃ thaṃ taṃ ṇaṃ ḍhaṃ ḍaṃ ṭhaṃ ṭaṃ ñaṃ jhaṃ jaṃ chaṃ*.

Having filled the jar with the causal [substance] while reciting the root mantra as the reverse alphabet (vilomamātṛkā): *caṃ ṅaṃ ghaṃ gaṃ khaṃ kaṃ aṃḥ aṃ auṃ oṃ aiṃ eṃ ḹṃ ḷṃ ṝṃ ṛṃ ūṃ uṃ īṃ iṃ āṃ aṃ*. Thus. *uṃ*.

"Obeisance to the lunar maṇḍala, whose self consists of sixteen digits. Having thus worshipped the causal source, [one should invoke] the lunar maṇḍala with the mantra "Kroṃ Gaṅge ca," etc., using the *aṅkuśa-mudrā*. There, one should invite the sacred waters (*tīrthas*) and bow down with the five mudrās. Placing both palms upon the ground, [one recites] "Drāṃ..."

*Namaḥ*. Thus, with the *catusrā* [mudrā], placing both hands in a hollowed shape (*puṭākāra*) upon the ground, [one recites]: *drāṃ namaḥ*. Thus, with the *saṃvṛtā* [mudrā], with the hollowed palms (*puṭāñjali*) upon the ground, [one recites]: *klīṃ namaḥ*. Thus, with the *saṃpūṭā* [mudrā], with the palms joined upon the ground such that the two little fingers are placed at their bases and the other fingers are extended, [one recites]: *blūṃ namaḥ*. Thus.

(4) The one called *puṭāñjali*: Having placed the *yonimudrā* on the ground, [one says] "Oṃ *namaḥ*. This is the one called *yoni*. Thus is the prostration with the five mudrās. Then, one should perform the *pañcīkaraṇa* as follows: *phaṭ*—striking with a blade of *darbha* grass; *huṃ*—veiling; *namaḥ*—inspecting with the root mantra.

Thus is the sprinkling with water for the arghya offering (4). One should smell the fragrance three times with the root mantra. Then, having placed a flower in the pitcher with "Oṃ," one should consecrate it three times with the Brahmā-ṛc as follows:
"Oṃ haṃ saḥ, the pure-dwelling Vasu, dwelling in the mid-region, the Hotṛ-priest, dwelling on the altar, dwelling in the firmament, dwelling in the house."
The truth-born, the great Truth, born of the mountain, born of the cow, born of the sacrifice, like the slayer of the untruthful, the best of those who dwell in the truth—
therefrom one should perform the release from the curse:
*Oṃ, the Supreme Brahman alone is the eternal, consisting of the gross and the subtle.*
Therefore, I shall destroy that sin of Brahman-slaughter born from your hair.
Thus three times. Oṃ! O Goddess, born from the solar disc, arisen from the abode of Varuṇa, composed of the seed-syllable Amā—be released from the curse of Śukra.
Thus three times. Oṃ: If the Praṇava is the seed of the Vedas and consists of the bliss of Brahman, by that truth, O Goddess, may it remove my sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa.
Thus three times.
*Oṃ vāṃ vīṃ vūṃ vaiṃ vauṃ vaḥ*, obeisance to the Goddess Sudhā, who is liberated from the curse of Brahmā; thus ten times.

Oṃ śāṃ śīṃ śūṃ śaiṃ śauṃ śaḥ, obeisance to the Goddess Sudhā, who is liberated from the curse of Śukra. Thus is the tenfold liberation from the curse of Śukra. Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kroṃ krīṃ krūṃ kraiṃ krauṃ kraḥ, liberate [this] from the curse of Kṛṣṇa regarding the nectar. (2)
"Make [it] nectar, svāhā! Thus, [recite] the curse of Kṛṣṇa twelve times.

"Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, we know Ānandeśvara; we meditate upon Sudhādevī; may that Lord who is half-woman-and-half-man inspire us. Thus, one should recite the Ānanda-gāyatrī three times. Then, in the midst of the substances...

One should draw the power-maṇḍala of Akathādi as follows: sixteen lines beginning with *ā* on the left, sixteen lines beginning with *ka* above, and sixteen lines beginning with *tha* on the right. In the triangles, one should write *haṃ*, *laṃ*, and *kṣaṃ*;
likewise, all the letters joined with the bindu (*m*) should be written, and in the center, one should write the seed-syllable *hsauṃ*. [The mantra: *hsauḥ maṇḍalāya*.
Salutation! Having thus worshipped the mandala, one should meditate there upon Ānandabhairava and Ānandabhairavī:
the god who resembles ten million suns and is as cool as ten million moons, possessing eighteen arms, five faces, and three eyes.
Seated in the midst of the ocean of nectar, resting upon the lotus of Brahman,
mounted upon his bull, the blue-throated one adorned with all ornaments.
The god holds a skull and a khaṭvāṅga staff, possesses bells, hand-drums, and so forth,
and carries a noose, a goad, a mace, and a club.
He holds a sword, a shield, a paṭṭiśa, a mallet, a trident, and a staff;
he carries a variegated shield and a severed head, and his hands display the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.
The best of practitioners should meditate upon Lohita, the Lord of the Gods of gods. Having thus visualized him, he should recite the mantra: *hasakṣamalavarayūṃ ānandabhairavāya vaṣaṭ*.
Then, having worshipped three times with the words: "These perfumes and flowers are for Ānandabhairava; obeisance," he should offer them.
One should meditate upon Ānandabhairavī.
One should contemplate the Goddess as the Nectar (Sudhā), possessing the radiance of ten million times ten thousand moons,
white as snow, kunda flowers, and the moon, with five faces and three eyes.
Endowed with eighteen arms, intent on bestowing all bliss,
smiling, large-eyed, and facing the God of gods.

Having meditated thus, one should recite the mantra: *sahakṣamalavarayīṃ ānandabhairavyai vauṣaṭ*. Then, one should worship three times, saying: "These perfumes and flowers are for Ānandabhairavī; *namaḥ*. [Then recite: *īṃ krīṃ paramasvāmini paramākāśaśūnyavāhini candrasūryāgnibhakṣiṇi pātraṃ*.

"Viśa svāhā. Thus three times. "Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aiṃ, O Amṛte, O Amṛtodbhave, O Amṛtavarṣiṇi, O Mahatprakāśayukte, cause the nectar to flow, svāhā. Thus three times. With the mantras *Yaṃ Raṃ Vaṃ*, one should perform the drying, burning, and nectarification (*amṛtīkaraṇa*) of the substance. Then, with *Huṃ*.

Having veiled [the offering] with the *dhenumudrā*, rendered it nectarine with the *matsyamudrā*, and covered it, one should recite the seed-syllable of Varuṇa, *vaṃ*, eight times and the root mantra eight times there; this is the purification of the cause (*kāraṇaśuddhi*). Then, having placed meat, fish, *mudrā*, and *kulakusuma* flowers upon a mandala consisting of a triangle, a circle, and a square;

One should purify each [ingredient] individually. *Oṃ pratyadviṣṇustavate vīryeṇa mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhāḥ ugro yaḥ triṣu vikrameṣv adhikṣipanti bhuvanāni viśvā.* Thus is the purification of meat.
Oṃ, we worship Tryambaka, the fragrant one who increases prosperity;
may he deliver us from death as a cucumber is released from its stem, yet not from immortality.
Thus is the purification of the fish.
Oṃ, the heroic ones ever behold that supreme abode of Viṣṇu, like an eye extended in the sky.
Oṃ, the wise sages, ever vigilant, kindle that supreme abode of Viṣṇu which the inspired poets perceive.
Thus is the purification of the mudrās.
Oṃ, may Viṣṇu prepare the womb; may Tvaṣṭṛ fashion the forms; may Prajāpati pour [the seed]; may Dhātṛ place the embryo within me.
Oṃ! May Sinīvālī bestow the embryo; may Sarasvatī bestow the embryo.
May the two divine Aśvins, adorned with garlands of flowers, establish the embryo within you.
Glūṃ nlūṃ slūṃ plūṃ slūṃ, O Immortal One, O Source of Nectar, O Mistress of Nectar, O Showerer of Nectar, cause the nectar to flow! Svāhā! Thus is the purification of the Kula-flower.
Now, the purification of the *śakti* is as follows:

If the *śakti* has not been consecrated, one should sprinkle the *śakti* with the *arghya* water while reciting "phaṭ," veil it with "hūṃ," display the *yonimudrā*, and [perform] the *ṛṣi*-mantra and so forth upon its limbs.

Having performed the ritual placements (*nyāsa*) with "Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, obeisance to Tripurā; make this [woman] my Śakti, make her so, svāhā," one should cause the seed-syllable *hrīṃ* to be heard three times in her left ear. One should then recite the root mantra ten times upon her head.
If she has been instructed and consecrated, he himself should perform the *nyāsa* and other rites for her chosen deity;

this is the purification of power (*śaktiśuddhi*). Then, having dried away each [impurity] with the seed-syllable *yaṃ*, having burned it with the fire-seed-syllable *raṃ*, and having turned it into nectar with the *dhenumudrā* using *vaṃ*, [he should strike it] with *hūṃ*.

Having veiled [the vessel], again having rendered it nectar-like by means of the *dhenumudrā* with the syllable *vaṃ*, having kindled it with the root mantra using the *yonimudrā*, and having performed the ritual integration (*sakalīkaraṇa*) with the six limbs, one should cover it with the *matsyamudrā*.
Having recited the root mantra ten times over each of those [substances], one should arrange them in other vessels; such is the purification beginning with the initial cleansing.
Then, one should perform the installation of the Śrīpātra as follows:
between oneself and the Yantra, having drawn a mandala consisting of a triangle, a circle, a hexagon, and a square with "Hūṃ" in its center;
having sprinkled it with the water of the Arghya while reciting "Phaṭ"; [one should place the vessels] in the squares starting from the east.
Having worshipped in clockwise order with: "Oṃ, obeisance to Urdhvapāda; Pūṃ, obeisance to Pūrṇaśaula;
Jāṃ, obeisance to Jāleṃdhara; Kāṃ, obeisance to Kāmarūpa," and having worshipped the six limbs in the six corners, [one should worship] in the triangles.

Having recited the first section of the root mantra, [say] "Salutation to the principle of the self (ātmatattva). Having recited the second section, [say] "Salutation to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva).
Having recited the third section, [say] "Salutation to the principle of Śiva (śivatattva). In the center, [place] "Hūṃ, to the Support-Energy (ādhāraśakti)."

Saying "Namaḥ," having worshipped the mandala, and saying "Phaṭ," having washed the seat for the Śrīpātra, and saying "Namaḥ," having placed it upon the mandala; there, having drawn a mandala consisting of a triangle, a circle, and a hexagon, one should worship the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) within the hexagon.

Having worshipped the triangle with the root mantra, one should worship the ten kalās of Fire—starting from the east and proceeding clockwise upon the circle—with the following: *Yaṃ* *dhūmrārciṣe namaḥ*; *Raṃ* *ūṣmāyai namaḥ*;
*Laṃ* *jvalinyai namaḥ*; *Vaṃ* *jvālinyai namaḥ*; *Śaṃ* *visphuliṅginyai namaḥ*; *Ṣaṃ*.
Salutation to Suśrī; salutation to Saṃsurūpī; *haṃ*, salutation to Kapilā; *laṃ*, salutation to Havyavahā;
*kṣaṃ*, salutation to Kavyavahā. Above that, having worshipped with: "Salutation to the Fire-maṇḍala consisting of ten kalās, *maṃ*. Then, [cleansing] the vessel such as the great conch with "phaṭ."

Having washed [the vessel] with "Oṃ Namo," and having placed it upon the support (ādhāra), one should draw a triangle, a circle, and a hexagon there. Having worshipped the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) in the hexagon with the root mantra, and having worshipped the triangle as before, one should worship the twelve kalās of the Sun upon the circle: Kaṃ, Bhaṃ...

TAPINYAI NAMAḤ | KHAṂ VAṂ TĀPINYAI NAMAḤ | GAṂ PHAṂ DHŪMRĀYAI NAMAḤ | GHAṂ PAṂ MARĪCYAI NAMAḤ | ṄAṂ NAṂ JVĀLINYAI NAMAḤ | CAṂ DHAṂ RUCYAI NAMAḤ | CHAṂ DAṂ SUṢUMNĀYAI NAMAḤ | JAṂ THAṂ BHOGADĀYAI NAMAḤ |

*Namaḥ*. Jhaṃ taṃ, *namaḥ* to Viśvā. Ñaṃ ṇaṃ, *namaḥ* to Bodhinī. Ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ, *namaḥ* to Dhāriṇī. Ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ, *namaḥ* to Kṣamā. Above that, *aṃ*, *namaḥ* to the Solar Maṇḍala consisting of twelve kalās. Having thus worshipped, [worship] from the letter *kṣa* down to the letter *a*.
Having recited the *mātṛkā* in reverse order and the root mantra (*mūlamantra*), fill the *śrīpātra* in three parts with the liquid from the jar;
fill the remainder with water, and thereupon draw a triangle, a circle, and a hexagon.
Having worshipped the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) in the hexagon and the triangle with the root mantra, [perform] upon the circle as before.
One should worship the sixteen digits (*kalā*) of the Moon: *Am*—salutation to Amṛtā. *Ām*—salutation to Mānadā.
*Im*—salutation to Pūṣā. *Īm*—salutation to Tuṣṭi. *Um*—salutation to Puṣṭi. *Ūm*—salutation to Rati.
*Ṛm*—salutation to Dhṛti. *Ṝm*—salutation to Śaśinī. *Ḷm*—salutation to Candrikā. *Ḹm*...
Salutation to Kānti. Eṃ, salutation to Jyotsnā. Aiṃ, salutation to Śrī. Oṃ, salutation to Prīti.

Auṃ, salutation to Aṅgā. Aṃ, salutation to Pūrṇā. Aṃḥ, salutation to Pūrṇāmṛtā. Above that, having worshipped with: Uṃ, salutation to the lunar maṇḍala, whose self consists of sixteen kalās. Thus, one should worship.

There, having invoked the sacred ford (*tīrtha*) from the lunar disc with the mantra beginning "Kroṃ Gaṅge" and the *aṅkuśa* mudrā, one should cast red flowers, white and red sandalwood paste, *dūrvā* grass, and unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*) therein. Then, performing purification with the root mantra and the *mīna* mudrā, one should cast a few *kulakusuma* flowers there as before. [The sequence] begins with *a*, *ka*, and *ṭha*.

Having drawn the Śakti-maṇḍala there, and having worshipped the maṇḍala with "Hsauḥ, obeisance to the maṇḍala," one should meditate upon and worship Ānandabhairava and Ānandabhairavī there, as before.

Then, having taken up the Śrīpātra vessel, one should consecrate it with these mantras: Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ! Born from the essence of the cosmic egg, arising from the totality of essences, this great vessel is filled and brings forth the nectar of immortality.

Aiṃ! O you who bestow the bliss of the undivided single essence, O self of supreme nectar, O you whose manifestation is autonomous, O treasure of mantras, O you whose form is the Kula, place [this] within me!
Klīṃ! O you who abide in Akula, O you whose form is nectar, O you whose body is pure knowledge!
For immortality is indeed deposited in this reality that has a moist form.
Having achieved oneness with that form through the syllable *sauḥ*, O You whose nature is identical to that,
having become the very form of the Kula-nectar, perform Your emission within me.

Oṃ! May this [offering] not be a cause of distress; it is the supreme nectar. This act of acceptance is characterized by an oblation (*homa*) into the fire consisting of supreme *ahaṃtā*. Aiṃ! Speak, speak, O Goddess of Speech! Klīṃ! O Wet One, O Moistening One, moisten [me]! (2) Hsauḥ! Produce great agitation, produce it! Hsauṃḥ! Grant great liberation, grant it! Svāhā!

glūṃ slūṃ nlūṃ plūṃ mlūṃ, O Immortal One, O Source of Immortality, O Mistress of Immortality, O Showerer of Nectar, O You Endowed with Great Radiance, cause the nectar to flow, svāhā! Then, one should worship the five jewels in the Śrīpātra vessel: glūṃ, obeisance to those who reach the end of the sky; slūṃ...
Salutation to the jewels of heaven: *plūṃ* salutation to the jewels of the netherworld (*pātāla*). *mlūṃ* salutation to the jewels of the mortal world (*martya*).
Then, once again, one should worship Ānandabhairava and Ānandabhairavī there. Then, there—

Having invoked one's own chosen goddess (*iṣṭadevī*), having veiled her with "Hūṃ," having rendered her nectarine by means of the *dhenumudrā* with "Vaṃ," having inflamed her with the root mantra (*mūlamantra*) by means of the *yonimudrā*, having performed the ritual integration (*sakalīkaraṇa*) with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), and having covered her with the *matsyamudrā*,
one should recite the root mantra ten times there, [visualizing] the *śrīpātra* as the form of the Goddess.

Having meditated thus, one should worship the Goddess there with perfumes, flowers, incense, and lamps. With that water, one should sprinkle oneself and the ritual implements. This is the installation of the Śrīpātra.

Then one should place the vessels for the Guru and the others: near the jar, the vessel for the Guru; then the vessel for enjoyment (*bhogapātra*); then the vessel for the Śakti; then the vessel for the Yoginīs; then the vessel for the Vīras; then the vessel for the *bali* offering; then the vessel for water for the feet (*pādyapātra*). Then...

The vessel for sipping water (ācamanīpātra). With the *śrīpātra*, there are nine vessels. In its absence, there are seven vessels: the *śrīpātra*, the *gurupātra*, and the vessels for enjoyment (*bhoga*), the *śakti*, the *yoginī*, the hero (*vīra*), and the sacrificial offering (*bali*). In its absence, there are five vessels: the *śrīpātra*, the *gurupātra*, the *bhoga*, the *yoginī*, and the *bali*. In its absence, there are three vessels: the *śrīpātra*, the *gurupātra*, and the *bhoga*.
The sequence for their arrangement is as follows: having worshipped the triangular, circular, and square mandalas on the ground;
having washed the common vessels with "Phaṭ"; having placed them upon the mandala with "Namaḥ";
having filled the supporting vessels with the causal [liquid]; and [having placed] fire in the sacred waters.

Having worshipped the orbs of the sun and moon, one should place the *kulakusuma* flowers there with the *mīnamudrā* for purification; having veiled them with "Hūṃ," made them nectarine with the *dhenumudrā* and the syllable "Vaṃ," inflamed them with the root mantra and the *yonimudrā*, rendered them complete with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), and covered them with the *matsyamudrā*— therein...

One should recite the root mantra ten times. Then, one should perform the libation (*tarpaṇa*). As follows: with the *tattvamudrā* of the left hand, having taken the liquid from the *śrīpātra* together with the purification substances (*śuddhi*) and so forth, [one offers it] to the head with the mantra: *sahakṣamalavarayūṃ ānandabhairavāya vaṣaṭ*. This [is performed] along with the purification and the vessel.

"I offer libation to Ānandabhairava; obeisance. Having thus offered libation three times, [one should recite]: "To Ānandabhairavī, who possesses the syllables *sa-ha-ka-sa-ma-la-va-ra-yī*, *vaṣaṭ*. With this, along with purification and all things, I offer libation to Ānandabhairavī;
*svāhā*. Thus one should offer libation three times.

Then, with the nectar from the vessel of the Guru, [recite] thus: *Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, I satisfy the venerable sandals of Amukānandanātha and the venerable goddess Amukīdevī; obeisance.* [Recite this] three times. Then: *Aiṃ Śrīṃ, I satisfy the Guru; obeisance. Aiṃ, I satisfy the Paramaguru; obeisance. Aiṃ, I satisfy the Parāparaguru; obeisance.*

I satisfy [the deity], obeisance. Aiṃ, I satisfy the Supreme Guru, obeisance. With the nectar from the Śrīpātra: Oṃ, I satisfy the gods, obeisance. Oṃ, I satisfy the sages, obeisance. Oṃ, I satisfy the ancestors, obeisance. Thus, one should satisfy them once each. Then, having recited the root mantra with the nectar from the Śrīpātra, this...
"I satisfy the glorious Dakṣiṇakālikā along with the pure liquor; homage, svāhā!

Thus one should perform the libation seven times, five times, or three times. Then, with the nectar from the vessel of enjoyment, having recited the mantra of Mahākāla: "This [nectar] along with the pure liquor [is for] the glorious Mahākālabhairava..."
"I satisfy [you], obeisance. Thus, one should perform the libation three times.

Then, with the nectar from the *śakti*-vessel or the nectar from the *yoginī*-vessel, while reciting the root mantra: "This [nectar], together with the pure liquor, for [the deity] along with the weapons and the vehicle..."

"I offer libations to the glorious Dakṣiṇakālikā, together with her retinue and accompanied by the illustrious Mahākālabhairava; svāhā! Thus one should perform the libation three times. This is the rite of libation (*tarpaṇa*). Then, one should perform the purification of the principles (*tattvaśuddhi*).
With palms joined in reverence (*añjali*), [one recites]: "Oṃ, may my prāṇa, apāna, samāna, udāna, and vyāna be purified; I am light."
May I become free from passion and free from evil; svāhā! || 1 ||
Oṃ, may earth, water, fire, air, and space be purified for me; and so forth. || 2 ||
Oṃ, may my primordial nature, ego, intellect, mind, and ears be purified; and so forth. || 3 ||
Oṃ, may my skin, eyes, tongue, nose, and speech be purified, and so forth. || 4 ||
Oṃ, may my hands, feet, anus, genitals, and sense of hearing be purified; and so forth. || 5 ||
Oṃ, may my touch, form, taste, smell, and space be purified, and so forth.

Thus, having wiped [the hand] with the seven *ṛc*s for the purpose of purification, and having drawn a downward-facing triangle on the palm of the right hand, and having placed the *śuddhi-khaṇḍas* within the corners and the center of the triangle, [one recites] at the end of the root mantra: *hrīṃ śrīṃ ātmatattvena sthūladehaṃ śodhayāmi svāhā*.

With this [mantra] using the *bhagamudrā*, one should accept the purification situated below. At the end of the root mantra: *hrīṃ śrīṃ vidyātatvena sūkṣmadehaṃ śodhayāmi svāhā*. With this, one should accept the purification situated on the right. At the end of the root mantra: *hrīṃ śrīṃ śivatatvena paradehaṃ*...

"Śodhayāmi svāhā. With this, one should accept the purification residing on the left. At the end of the root mantra: "Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, by means of all the principles (tattvas), I purify the soul (jīva) which is the support of the body and the three [worlds], svāhā. With this, one should accept the purification residing in the center; this is the purification of the principles (tattva-śuddhi). Then, with the *bhogapātra* and the *tatvamudrā*...

One should perform the acceptance [of the offering] three times with the following: "The root is moist; it blazes. I am the light; the light blazes. I am Brahman; I am Brahman; I am that which I am; I am that which I am; I am Brahman. Indeed, I myself offer myself—svāhā! (1)
You alone are the root; having become the manifest Brahman, I shall speak to you alone.
May you protect me; may you protect the speaker; may you protect both me and the speaker. Svāhā! || 2 ||
The root, the supreme meter, the bull of all forms—He has arisen from the meters, from immortality. May He endow me with intelligence;
may I become a bearer of the immortal, O God. May the wise one dwell within my body; may my tongue [be swift].
O you who flow abundantly from both ears like one intoxicated by honey, you are the treasury of the Veda, covered with wisdom;
protect what I have heard—svāhā! || 3 ||
Thus, with these three mantras, the wise one should accept [the offerings] three times. Then, one should offer the *bali* to Vaṭuka and the others.

Having constructed four mandalas—triangular, circular, and square—in the directions starting from the east of the lion-throne; or else, having constructed a single mandala to one's left, [one should sprinkle it] with the water for the *arghya* while reciting "phaṭ."

Having sprinkled these scents and flowers with *saṃprokṣya*, and having worshipped the mandala with "Oṃ, obeisance to the mandala" (*oṃ maṇḍalāya namaḥ*), one should place there four offerings (*balicatuṣṭaya*) together with meat, fish, mudrās, vessels for the offerings, and other requisites. Then, in the east, having worshipped Vaṭuka with "These scents and flowers, obeisance to Vaṭuka" (*ete gandhapuṣpe vāṃ vaṭukāya namaḥ*).

Holding the *bali* offering with the *tattvamudrā* in the left hand, and taking water for the *arghya* or the liquid from the nine vessels in the right hand, one should present the *bali*: "Come, come, O Goddess! O Puṭa-vaṭukanātha!
You who possess a mass of tawny matted hair, you who are radiant, three-eyed, and flame-mouthed! Destroy, destroy all obstacles!"

"Take the offering, take the offering, svāhā! This offering is for Vaṭukanātha, obeisance! To the south, to the Yoginīs, obeisance! Having thus worshipped, taking the offering with the thumb and ring finger of the right hand, and holding either the *kāraṇa* substance or water with the left hand, one should cast forth the offering upward with this [mantra].
Whether in the cosmic egg, in the vault of heaven, on the surface of the earth, in the partless realm, or in the netherworld;
whether in a forest, in water, in the wind, or wherever else they may be situated;
or in sacred fields, seats, and secondary seats—may the Goddesses, who have performed their supreme rites with incense, lamps, and other offerings, be pleased.
May those who are worshipped by the lords of heroes protect us always with the rite of the auspicious offering (*śubhabali*). [Recite: *yāṃ yoginībhyaḥ svāhā*;
*sarvayoginībhyo huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. "This offering is for the Yoginīs; obeisance! In the west: *kṣāṃ kṣetrapālāya namaḥ*. Having thus worshipped as before, [form] the left fist...
Having made the index finger straight and holding the offering, one should release it. With this [mantra],
I worship the Protector of the Field (Kṣetrapālaka), who holds a trident, a hand-drum, a skull-cup, and a conch, and who is dark-complexioned.

*Kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣūṃ kṣaiṃ kṣauṃ kṣaḥ*, O guardian of the site and field (*sthānakṣetrapāla*), accept this *bali* offering accompanied by incense, lamps, and other articles; *svāhā*. This *bali* is for the Kṣetrapāla; obeisance. To the north:
*Gāṃ*, obeisance to Gaṇeśa. Having thus worshipped Gaṇeśa, [one should perform] the left-hand fist gesture.

One should offer the *bali* with the middle finger and thumb joined straightly, using this [mantra]: *gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaiṃ gauṃ gaḥ gaṇapataye varada sarvagaṃ naṃ me vaśamānaya baliṃ gṛhṇa svāhā*. This *bali* is for Gaṇeśa; *namaḥ*. Then, having drawn a square mandala on one's left, [one says] *phaṭ*.

Having sprinkled the maṇḍala with water and worshipped it with "Oṃ, to the all-pervading maṇḍala," one should place the bali offering there as before, reciting: "These perfumes and flowers, Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, for all obstructing spirits and all elemental beings, Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā! This is the bali."

Salutations to all beings! If one is unable to offer the five-fold oblation (*pañcabali*), one should offer a single oblation to all beings. This is the procedure for offering the oblation. Then, having performed breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) and the ritual placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*), [one should contemplate] oneself in the form of the *kāmakalā*.

One should meditate. One should contemplate the meditation upon this seed-syllable of Kāmakalā, *Īṃ*, [as] the beautiful goddess whose form pervades all. O Goddess of gods, the first face of the goddess consists of the four internal semi-vowels (*antaḥstha*) which have become the letter *I*, along with three *bindus*.
One should place two drops upon the pair of breasts at the location of the heart.
One should contemplate the subtle half-measure of the letter *ha* within the center of the womb,
likewise in the form of the *kāmakalā*, the range of the sprout of passion.
